pob.text: King David was old[a], advanced in days; and they covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.

spob.text: King David was very old. They covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.
public_domain_references.web: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.
public_domain_references.asv: Now king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.

public_domain_references.brenton: And king David [was] old and advanced in days, and they covered him with clothes, and he was not warmed.

pob.text: So his servants said to him[a], “Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin woman, and let her attend the king and be his caregiver, and let her lie in your bosom[c][b], so that my lord the king may be warm.”

spob.text: So his servants said to him, “Let them look for a young woman who is a virgin for my lord the king. Let her serve the king and care for him. Let her lie in your arms[a], so that my lord the king may be warm.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”

public_domain_references.brenton: And his servants said, Let them seek for the king a young virgin, and she shall wait on the king, and cherish him, and lie with him, and my lord the king shall be warmed.

pob.text: So they searched throughout all the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman[b][a], and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

spob.text: So they looked all across Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag from Shunem and brought her to the king.

public_domain_references.brenton: So they sought for a fair damsel out of all the coasts of Israel; and they found Abisag the Somanite, and they brought her to the king.

pob.text: The young woman was very beautiful[a], and she became the king’s attendant and served him, but the king did not know her.

spob.text: The young woman was very beautiful. She became the king’s attendant and served him. But the king did not have sexual relations with her.[a]

pob.text: Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself[a], saying, “I will reign.” So he made for himself a chariot, horsemen[b], and fifty men running before him.

pob.text: His father had never displeased him at any time by saying[a], “Why have you done thus?” He was also very handsome[b], and his mother had borne him after Absalom.

spob.text: His father had never challenged him by asking,[a] “Why did you do that?” He was also very handsome, and his mother gave birth to him after Absalom was born.

pob.text: And he conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest[a], and they helped Adonijah.

pob.text: Adonijah sacrificed sheep[a], cattle, and fattened animals by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah[e][d][c][b], the king’s servants.

pob.text: Please go in to King David and say to him[a], ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, saying, “Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’

public_domain_references.web: All these were of costly stones, even of stone cut according to measure, sawed with saws, inside and outside, even from the foundation to the coping, and so on the outside to the great court.
public_domain_references.asv: All these were of costly stones, even of hewn stone, according to measure, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside unto the great court.
public_domain_references.kjv: All these [were of] costly stones, according to the measures of hewed stones, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and [so] on the outside toward the great court.
public_domain_references.brenton: and a chamber over both the pillars, and above the sides an addition [equal to] the chamber in width.

pob.text: And the foundation was of costly stones[a], large stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.

spob.text: The foundation was built with large, costly stones.[a] Some stones measured ten cubits, and others measured eight cubits.

public_domain_references.bsb: The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
public_domain_references.web: The foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
public_domain_references.asv: And the foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the foundation [was of] costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he made the sea, ten cubits from one rim to the other, the same was completely circular round about: its height [was] five cubits, and its circumference thirty-three cubits.

pob.text: And above were costly stones[a], cut according to measure, and cedar.

spob.text: The upper part was made of costly stones cut to size, along with cedar wood.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Above these were high-grade stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
public_domain_references.web: Above were costly stones, even cut stone, according to measure, and cedar wood.
public_domain_references.asv: And above were costly stones, even hewn stone, according to measure, and cedar-wood.
public_domain_references.kjv: And above [were] costly stones, after the measures of hewed stones, and cedars.
public_domain_references.brenton: And stays underneath its rim round about compassed it ten cubits round;

pob.text: And the great court all around had three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams[c][b][a], like the inner court of the house of Yahweh and the vestibule of the house.

spob.text: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams. It was built like the inner courtyard of Yahweh’s temple and the temple’s entrance hall.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: The great court around had three courses of cut stone with a course of cedar beams, like the inner court of Yahweh’s house and the porch of the house.
public_domain_references.asv: And the great court round about had three courses of hewn stone, and a course of cedar beams; like as the inner court of the house of Jehovah, and the porch of the house.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the great court round about [was] with three rows of hewed stones, and a row of cedar beams, both for the inner court of the house of the LORD, and for the porch of the house.
public_domain_references.brenton: and its rim [was ] as the work of the rim of a cup, a lily-flower, and the thickness of it [was ] a span.

pob.text: Then King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

spob.text: King Solomon sent for Hiram and had him brought from Tyre.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
public_domain_references.web: King Solomon sent and brought Hiram out of Tyre.
public_domain_references.asv: And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [there were] twelve oxen under the sea; three looking to the north, and three looking to the west, and three looking to the south, and three looking to the east: and all their hinder parts [were] inward, and the sea [was] above upon them.

pob.text: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali[a], and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to do every kind of work in bronze[b]. So he came to King Solomon and did all his work.

spob.text: His mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was from Tyre and was a skilled bronze worker.[a] He was filled with the wisdom, understanding, and knowledge needed for every kind of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.

public_domain_references.bsb: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
public_domain_references.web: He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill to work all works in bronze. He came to King Solomon and performed all his work.
public_domain_references.asv: He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill, to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.
public_domain_references.kjv: He [was] a widow’s son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father [was] a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he made ten brazen bases: five cubits [was] the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth of it, and its height [was] six cubits.

pob.text: He cast the two bronze pillars; the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits[a], and a line of twelve cubits measured around it.

spob.text: He cast the two bronze pillars. One pillar was eighteen cubits high (about 27 feet or 8 meters), and a cord twelve cubits long (about 18 feet or 5.5 meters) went around it.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
public_domain_references.web: For he fashioned the two pillars of bronze, eighteen cubits high apiece; and a line of twelve cubits encircled either of them.
public_domain_references.asv: For he fashioned the two pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of twelve cubits compassed either of them about.
public_domain_references.kjv: For he cast two pillars of brass, of eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of twelve cubits did compass either of them about.
public_domain_references.brenton: And this work of the bases [was] formed with a border to them, and [there was] a border between the ledges.

pob.text: He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of the one capital was five cubits[a], and the height of the second capital was five cubits.

spob.text: He made two decorative tops of cast bronze to place on top of the pillars. Each one was about seven and a half feet (2.3 meters) high.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.

public_domain_references.brenton: And upon their borders between the projections [were] lions, and oxen, and cherubs: and on the projections, even so above, and also below [were] the places of lions and oxen, hanging work.

pob.text: There were lattices of latticework and twisted cords of chainwork for the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars: seven for the one capital[a], and seven for the second capital.

spob.text: There were latticework decorations and twisted cords made like chains for the decorative tops of the pillars. There were seven for one pillar top and seven for the other.[a]

public_domain_references.kjv: [And] nets of checker work, and wreaths of chain work, for the chapiters which [were] upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one chapiter, and seven for the other chapiter.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [there were] four brazen wheels to one base; and [there were] brazen bases, and their four sides [answering to them], side pieces under the bases.

pob.text: He made the pillars[a], and two rows all around on the one latticework, to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates[b]; and so he did for the second capital.

spob.text: He made the pillars. On one latticework, he made two rows all around it to cover the decorative pillar tops that were on top of the pomegranate-shaped ornaments. He made the second pillar top in the same way.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.

public_domain_references.asv: So he made the pillars; and there were two rows round about upon the one network, to cover the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars: and so did he for the other capital.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he made the pillars, and two rows round about upon the one network, to cover the chapiters that [were] upon the top, with pomegranates: and so did he for the other chapiter.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [there were] axles in the wheels under the base. And the height of one wheel [was] a cubit and a half.

pob.text: And the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars were made like a lily blossom in the portico[c][b][a], four cubits.

spob.text: The capitals—the top sections of the pillars at the temple entrance—were shaped like lily blossoms.[b] The text gives a measurement of four cubits (about six feet), but does not say which dimension this measures.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the chapiters that [were] upon the top of the pillars [were] of lily work in the porch, four cubits.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the work of the wheels [was] as the work of chariot wheels: their axles, and their felloes, and [the rest of] their work, [were] all molten.

pob.text: And the capitals were on the two pillars[a], also above, opposite the bulge that was beside the latticework; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around[c][b], on the second capital.

spob.text: The capitals—the decorated tops of the two pillars—were also above and opposite the rounded bulge beside the latticework. Two hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments were arranged in rows all around the second capital.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
public_domain_references.web: There were capitals above also on the two pillars, close by the belly which was beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows around the other capital.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the chapiters upon the two pillars [had pomegranates] also above, over against the belly which [was] by the network: and the pomegranates [were] two hundred in rows round about upon the other chapiter.
public_domain_references.brenton: The four side-pieces were at the four corners of each base; its shoulders [were formed] of the base.

pob.text: He set up the pillars at the portico of the temple[a]. He set up the right pillar and called its name Jachin; then he set up the left pillar and called its name Boaz.

spob.text: He set up the pillars at the temple’s front porch. He set up the pillar on the right and named it Jachin. Then he set up the pillar on the left and named it Boaz.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
public_domain_references.web: He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He set up the right pillar and called its name Jachin; and he set up the left pillar and called its name Boaz.

public_domain_references.kjv: And he set up the pillars in the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Jachin: and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
public_domain_references.brenton: And on the top of the base half a cubit [was] the size of it, [there was] a circle on the top of the base, and [there was] the top of its spaces and its borders: and it was open at the top of its spaces.

pob.text: And on the top of the pillars was lily-work[b][a], and the work of the pillars was finished.

spob.text: The tops of the pillars were decorated with lily designs. Then the work on the pillars was finished.

public_domain_references.bsb: And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.
public_domain_references.web: On the tops of the pillars was lily work. So the work of the pillars was finished.
public_domain_references.asv: And upon the top of the pillars was lily-work: so was the work of the pillars finished.
public_domain_references.kjv: And upon the top of the pillars [was] lily work: so was the work of the pillars finished.
public_domain_references.brenton: And its borders [were] cherubs, and lions, and palm-trees, upright, each [was] joined in front [and] within and round about.

pob.text: Then he made the cast sea[a], ten cubits from brim to brim, round all around; its height was five cubits[c][b], and a line of thirty cubits went around it all around.

spob.text: Then he made the large cast-metal basin called the Sea.[a] It was circular, ten cubits across from brim to brim and five cubits high. Its circumference was thirty cubits.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
public_domain_references.web: He made the molten sea ten cubits from brim to brim, round in shape. Its height was five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits encircled it.

public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And he made a molten sea, ten cubits from the one brim to the other: [it was] round all about, and his height [was] five cubits: and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about.
public_domain_references.brenton: According to the same form he made all the ten bases, [even] one order and one measure to all.

pob.text: And gourds were under its rim all around[a], encircling it, ten to the cubit, surrounding the Sea all around. The gourds were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.

spob.text: Under its rim, two rows of gourd-shaped decorations[a] ran all the way around the large basin called the Sea. There were ten decorations along each cubit (roughly half a meter) of its circumference. They were cast in one piece with the basin.

public_domain_references.bsb: Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
public_domain_references.web: Under its brim around there were buds which encircled it for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The buds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.

public_domain_references.kjv: And under the brim of it round about [there were] knops compassing it, ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about: the knops [were] cast in two rows, when it was cast.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he made ten brazen lavers, each laver containing forty baths, [and] measuring four cubits, each laver [placed] on a several base throughout the ten bases.

pob.text: It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north[a], three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east; and the Sea was on them above[b], and all their rear parts were inward.

spob.text: It stood on twelve oxen. Three faced north, three west, three south, and three east. The Sea rested on top of them, and all their rear parts pointed inward.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
public_domain_references.web: It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea was set on them above, and all their hindquarters were inward.

public_domain_references.brenton: And he put five bases on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and the sea was placed on the right side of the house eastward in the direction of the south.

pob.text: Its thickness was a handbreadth[a], and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom[b]. It could hold two thousand baths.

spob.text: Its walls were one handbreadth thick—about the width of a hand. Its rim was shaped like a cup’s rim and a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.
public_domain_references.web: It was a hand width thick. Its brim was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.
public_domain_references.asv: And it was a handbreadth thick: and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it held two thousand baths.
public_domain_references.kjv: And it [was] an hand breadth thick, and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies: it contained two thousand baths.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Chiram made the caldrons, and the pans, and the bowls; and Chiram finished making all the works that he wrought for king Solomon in the house of the Lord:

pob.text: He made ten bronze stands. The length of each stand was four cubits[a], its width four cubits, and its height three cubits.

spob.text: He made ten bronze stands.[a] Each one was about six feet long, six feet wide, and four and a half feet high.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
public_domain_references.web: He made the ten bases of bronze. The length of one base was four cubits, four cubits its width, and three cubits its height.

public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And he made ten bases of brass; four cubits [was] the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth thereof, and three cubits the height of it.
public_domain_references.brenton: two pillars and the wreathen works of the pillars on the heads of the two pillars; and the two net-works to cover both the wreathen works of the flutings that were upon the pillars.

pob.text: And this was the construction of the stand: they had frames[b][a], and there were frames between the supports.

spob.text: This is how each stand was built: it had frames, with frames between the supports.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,

pob.text: And the one stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles[a], and its four corners had supports for them; beneath the basin the supports were cast[c][b], each beside wreathwork.

pob.text: Its opening projected upward from within the capital by a cubit[a], and its opening was round, like the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half; and also on its opening were carvings, and their panels were square[c][b], not round.

It was round, like the work of a pedestal, and was one and a half cubits (about 27 inches or 68 centimeters).[a] There were also carvings on the opening,[b] and its panels were square, not round.

pob.text: The workmanship of the wheels was like the workmanship of a chariot wheel[a]; their axles, their rims, their spokes[b], and their hubs were all cast metal.

pob.text: But as for you[a], arise, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

pob.text: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him[a], because he alone of Jeroboam’s house will come to the grave, since in him something good toward Yahweh, the God of Israel[c][b], has been found in the house of Jeroboam.

pob.text: And Yahweh will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam this day[a]. But what? Even now.

spob.text: Yahweh will bring his own king to power over Israel. This king will cut off Jeroboam’s royal house this very day.[a] But what? Even now.

public_domain_references.bsb: Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day—yes, even today!

pob.text: And Yahweh will strike Israel[a], as a reed sways in the water, and he will uproot Israel from this good land that he gave to their fathers, and scatter them beyond the River, because they made their Asherim[b], provoking Yahweh.

spob.text: Yahweh will strike Israel, making it sway like a reed in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the River[a]. This will happen because they made their Asherah poles, provoking Yahweh.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: For the LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that He gave their fathers, and He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking the LORD to anger.
public_domain_references.web: For Yahweh will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water; and he will root up Israel out of this good land which he gave to their fathers, and will scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking Yahweh to anger.

pob.text: And he will give up Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam[a], which he committed and by which he caused Israel to sin.

pob.text: Then Jeroboam’s wife arose and went and came to Tirzah. As she came to the threshold of the house[a], the boy died.

pob.text: They buried him[a], and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of Yahweh that he had spoken through his servant Ahijah the prophet.

pob.text: The rest of the acts of Jeroboam[a], how he fought and how he reigned, behold[c][b], they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

pob.text: The days that Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. Then he lay down with his fathers[a], and Nadab his son became king in his place.

spob.text: Jeroboam was king for twenty-two years. Then he lay down with his ancestors[a], and his son Nadab became king in his place.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the days which Jeroboam reigned [were] two and twenty years: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

pob.text: Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah[a]. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that Yahweh had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put his name there[b]. And his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite woman.

spob.text: Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, ruled in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem. Yahweh had chosen Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel as the special place for his presence and worship.[a] Rehoboam’s mother was Naamah, an Ammonite woman.

spob.text: Cult prostitutes were also present in the land.[a] They followed all the detestable practices of the nations Yahweh had driven out before the sons of Israel.

pob.text: Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold[a], but they did not go[b], because the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.

pob.text: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father[b][a], and Jehoram his son became king in his place.

spob.text: Jehoshaphat died.[a] He was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, named for his forefather David. Then his son Jehoram became king in his place.

pob.text: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

spob.text: During Jehoshaphat’s seventeenth year as king of Judah, Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria. He ruled Israel for two years.
